extracted.intended_audience: public housing authorities (PHAs), multifamily housing owners/operators, landlords, and stakeholders commenting on HUD rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and HUD responses to public comments about a proposed rule requiring a 30-day notice for lease termination for nonpayment of rent in HUD-assisted housing; focuses on legal authority, notice content, implementation timelines, financial impacts, and mitigation options for housing providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's statutory authority to prescribe lease terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary has explicit statutory and regulatory authority to require that certain terms and conditions be included within leases for HUD-assisted housing, including specified notice periods and other procedural protections before different types of eviction proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites consistent past exercises of authority (e.g., interim final rules, Smoke-Free Public Housing rule, HUD grievance procedures). Notes that owners are not required to participate in HUD programs but that participation carries obligations; courts have upheld HUD's ability to ensure due process in eviction processes for HUD participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory content of the nonpayment notice
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered in compliance, the notice must include instructions on how tenants can cure lease violations for nonpayment of rent; the alleged amount of rent owed by the tenant, and any other arrearages allowed by HUD and included in the lease; the date by which the tenant must pay rent to avoid the filing of an eviction; information on how tenants can recertify their income; how tenants can request a minimum rent hardship exemption, if applicable, or request to switch from flat rent to income-based rent; and in the event of a Presidential declaration of a national emergency, such information as required by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD reiterates these elements are required for compliance. The rule focuses on notification requirements; repayment plans are encouraged but not required. HUD may issue models/guidance to assist inclusion of required language in notices and leases.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day notification period balances tenant cure opportunity and PHA financial impact
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD believes the 30-day notification period strikes an appropriate balance that considers the financial obligations of PHAs and owners, as well as provides enough time for tenants to rectify a lease violation stemming from nonpayment of rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD's rationale: delays can enable tenants to cure arrears (sometimes due to recertification errors or one-time events) and can prevent unnecessary eviction filings; HUD estimates between 1,600 and 4,900 nonpayment-related moveouts in Public Housing and PBRA-assisted housing are prevented each year because of the 30-day requirement. HUD acknowledges financial impacts but judges the balance appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: HUD lacks authority to reimburse owners after tenancy termination or during evictions
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD program statutes and regulations only authorize assistance payments for dwelling units under lease by eligible families; HUD does not have the authority to make assistance payments, pay contract rent, or otherwise reimburse owners after the termination of tenancy or during eviction proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD encourages PHAs experiencing shortfalls to apply for the Shortfall fund. For Multifamily Housing programs, owners may submit special claims per program regulations for unpaid tenant rent or other amounts owed under the lease, but there is no special claims provision for lost rent accrued while a tenant continues to reside in a unit after termination of tenancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Shortfall fund and special claims procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs experiencing significant shortfalls in their operating budgets are encouraged to apply for the Shortfall fund; in applicable Multifamily Housing programs an owner can submit a special claims request for unpaid tenant rent or other amounts owed under the lease in accordance with program regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that these are the program-specific remedies HUD can offer; clarifies limits (no special claims for lost rent while tenant remains occupying the unit after termination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification procedures and staff responsibilities to reduce improper arrears
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs and owners should improve compliance with recertification requirements by ensuring staff do not transfer burdens of recertification onto tenants, properly and timely inform tenants of different verification options, avoid requiring more verification than necessary from tenants, and seek verifications that staff can obtain themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD asserts that better recertification practices reduce improper overcharges and arrearages; encourages PHAs/owners to review policies and practices to facilitate on-time recertifications, rental payments, or timely repayment plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and encouragement for repayment plans
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD strongly encourages but does not require the use of repayment plans; PHAs and owners have flexibility to design reasonable repayment agreements as one way for tenants to cure nonpayment of rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repayment plans are emphasized as cost-effective compared to eviction filings. HUD reiterates repayment plans are optional and that the final rule focuses particularly on notification requirements rather than mandating repayment agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timeline for lease amendments and model leases
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD is not requiring PHAs and owners to update leases at once; PHAs must amend leases within 18 months of the effective date of the rule, and for PBRAs, within 14 months from the date HUD publishes a final model lease incorporating the new requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD will produce model leases for PBRA programs incorporating HOTMA and this rule's changes and may provide additional guidance to assist implementation; this timeline is intended to minimize administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of administrative burden and procedural flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD recognizes burdens created by new requirements (e.g., revising formal policies, amending every lease, training staff, modifying computerized systems) and states the rule is designed to minimize impacts on housing providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD's measures include phased timelines for lease amendments, model leases for PBRA, potential future guidance, and not requiring immediate, simultaneous changes; HUD acknowledges small PHAs and resource constraints and that implementation will require staff time and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHAS/TAR scoring impacts and temporary relief measures
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD agrees PHAs should not be penalized as a result of compliance with this rule and acknowledges that the extended notification period may affect PHAs' financial assessment scores if TARs (tenant accounts receivable) rise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD has provided relief to PHAs for PHAS scoring of TARs for 2022 and 2023 and is evaluating further extensions based on data; HUD is developing a proposed rule on the Public Housing Assessment Systems (PHAS) anticipated to be published later in 2024 and encourages comments on that rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual responsibility for tenant awareness and timely recertification
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a mutual responsibility between tenants and PHAs/owners to ensure recertification requirements are followed; notice requirements help tenants who are unaware or remind those who are aware of ways to cure nonpayment of rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD underscores importance of PHAs/owners working with tenants to identify opportunities to improve practices and procedures (e.g., informing tenants about recertification options, hardship exemptions, and how to apply) that facilitate on-time recertifications and repayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of local eviction court delays but not a basis to negate notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD does not dictate local court timelines and disagrees that increasing the notification period merely delays evictions; HUD maintains that the 30-day notice can prevent unnecessary filings and is cost-effective compared to prolonged court processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters provided examples of lengthy local eviction timelines (weeks to months, continuances, appeals, sheriff execution delays), HUD emphasizes that eviction costs and court backlog are reasons to work with tenants on cures rather than rely on litigation; HUD cites estimated prevented moveouts as supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on program participation and housing supply considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD believes the limited scope of the rule does not curb participation in HUD programs and that owners participating in HUD programs are typically mission-aligned; HUD seeks balance that does not overly burden PHAs and owners while also benefiting tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responds to concerns that owners might exit HUD programs or that the rule would reduce affordable housing supply by noting voluntary participation and incentives, and asserting the rule's narrow focus limits negative impacts on participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data monitoring and evidence-based evaluation of TAR trends
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD monitors trends in tenant accounts receivable (TARs) and believes most PHAs are starting to experience lower TARs toward pre-pandemic levels though there are outliers keeping TARs elevated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD uses data monitoring to justify the rule's impacts and to determine potential further scoring relief; HUD cites monitoring and future proposed PHAS rulemaking as mechanisms to address scoring/financial impacts.
